messages:
support-jen: Heads up — ACME reported a p95 jump from ~120ms -> ~1.2s for text generation in us-west2 after last night's infra push (GPU FW + CUDA update). Also seeing a few 500s and auth latency spikes. /cc @devon @mike

devon: oncall? :rotating_light: any alerts live?

oncall-bot: Alert: p95_api_latency > 800ms in us-west2 on route /v1/generate (detected 1767010000).

mike: I'm seeing sustained NVMe queue depth increases on the nodes in that pool. KV cache miss rate spiked at the same time. iostat shows ~75-85% util on nvme.

tess: can someone paste iostat / nvme-cli output from one of the affected hosts?

mike: (paste)
```
# iostat -x 1 3
Device            r/s     w/s   rkB/s   wkB/s  %util
nvme0n1         320.4  1800.1  1280.0  20480.0  82.3
...
# nvme-cli monitor
timestamp: 02:12:14 firmware-reset
io_timeout: 12
qdepth: 254
```

aria: dmesg on the same node shows repeated "nvme io timeout" and a firmware reset around 02:12UTC. kernel also logged blk-mq warnings. looks correlated with the FW roll.

devon: quick hypothesis: FW + CUDA combo changed IO patterns (more small random writes / metadata flushes from checkpointing + KMS/TLS write behavior) -> storage saturation -> tail latency up -> auth (KMS) handshakes slow -> retries amplify load.

support-jen: ACME provided a repro: single request with long context that used the KV cache heavily reliably produces the spike in us-west2 stage. They can reproduce on demand.

ryan: mitigation proposals: 1) shift traffic off the affected shard to eu shard, 2) enable stricter prefix caching for that model, 3) throttle embed calls per token temporarily, 4) rollback firmware on a small canary set.

mike: I'll kick off a canary rollback on 2 hosts and route 10% traffic to them. command I'm running: `kubectl -n infra set image node-deployer=redwood/node-agent:v2026-rollback && ./infra/rollout.sh --hosts host-232,host-233`

tess: also can try changing IO scheduler to noop and bumping queue depth on canary to see if performance improves: `echo noop > /sys/block/nvme0n1/queue/scheduler` and tune `nr_requests`. do with caution.

aria: note: recent kernel preempt settings from the same rollout might interact here. i'd avoid broad scheduler changes until canary proves safe. watch dmesg closely.

devon: plan: mike = canary rollback + routing; tess = collect per-node iostat/perf and try scheduler test on canary; aria = monitor kernel/dmesg and check driver logs; ryan = coordinate customer comms + traffic routing. i'll own the runbook updates.

support-jen: :thumbsup: I'll tell ACME we're triaging and might move traffic, ETA will be provided after canary results.

mike: canary started now, shifting 10% traffic. initial monitoring shows p95 on canary hosts ~140ms, remaining hosts still ~1.1s.

oncall-bot: Update: p95 on canary hosts 140ms, unaffected shard 1.1s.

ryan: if canary holds for 15m we'll expand rollback. temp fix also: enable model-level caching TTL 60s to cut KV amplification while we remediate.

devon: followups for RCA: include FW regression + NVMe queue amplification due to increased small IOs and TLS/KMS write amplification. propose rollout policy change: local stress test (nvme fio + kernel burn-in) before global firmware rollout, and require storage qdepth / iostat baseline check in canary.

support-jen: customer asked for ETA — if canary stays green we'll start broader rollback and traffic migration, estimate ~3 hours. i'll update them.

mike: continuing monitoring. will post logs and perf snapshots to the incident doc.

aria: one more data point — kernel shows increased preempt-reschedule activity right after the firmware reset, could explain scheduling jitter for IO threads. adding to RCA notes.

devon: great. keep replies short here while we run the canary. we'll reconvene if p95 doesn't start trending down across the shard.
